publicationStmt.p: Amores Project working transcription, 9 September 2026. Awaiting independent second source reading; not human scholarly approval.

handDesc.handNote: The main verse text is written in brown ink. Layout, visible signs and annotations are transcribed without assigning historical hands from colour alone. Long s and ordinary letter allographs are represented by standard Latin characters.

origin.p: The source manifest dates this composite manuscript to the 11th and 12th centuries. The catalogue date is not a date for every intervention.

surrogates.p: Actual source pages 384, 385, 386 were inspected at full resolution and in enlarged crops. Viewer page numbers are one-based indices into the manifest, not manuscript page labels. e-codices IIIF source manifest

projectDesc.p: All 70 extant verse positions were first-read directly from witness S images. Existing annotation rectangles are reproduced without modification. No reading is supplied from LL or another witness. Word spacing and couplet grouping are editorial. Independent second reading remains required.

correction.p: Visible letters are retained even where they differ from familiar readings. Tentative paleography is localized with unclear. A missing written initial is represented as gap, without inventing its decoration. Marginal annotations are not silently substituted into the verse. Ink colour alone does not establish an erased reading or historical hand.

normalization.p: u/v and e caudata follow visible source forms as far as practicable. Long s and ordinary letter allographs use standard characters. Combining macrons represent visible suspension/contraction bars schematically. Abbreviations are paired with defensible expansions in choice/abbr/expan; unexplained letters are not expanded merely to match a familiar edition. Special glyph approximations are declared in charDecl. Their form is typographic rather than a facsimile drawing.

punctuation.p: Visible stops are transcribed as schematic dots or colons. Modern punctuation is not supplied. Word spaces are editorial except where space explicitly records a significant physical separation.

segmentation.p: Every verse has a stable ID and a facs pointer to a rectangle on the correct manifest canvas. Annotation page values are interpreted through the manifest index. Physical page changes are pb elements within logical couplets where necessary. Source text beyond the poem is used to verify boundaries but not included as verse.

Full-page source inspection shows aligned regular verse initials, without systematic alternate-line indentation. Only the visibly inset second opening verse retains rend=indent; explicit initial spaces remain separate.

interpretation.p: All70 verses and the first-pass note queue were independently compared with the manuscript images. Observation notes record supported readings; uncertainty notes preserve unresolved source evidence without creating automatic user tasks. No human scholarly approval is implied.

char.desc: Curled suspension sign following q, schematic

revisionDesc.change: First image reading completed for all 70 extant verses on source pages 384, 385, 386. Prepared evidence notes for independent second review.

Independently read manuscript pp384–386 and all70 lines. Corrected Multa48, recorded omitted abbreviation evidence at6,14,33,35,45,57,65,66, and removed unsupported expansions at27/60. Retained localized uncertainty and all original image rectangles.
Removed editorial even-verse insets after independent full-page layout review. Verse text, notes, source zones and locally recorded initial spaces are unchanged.

div.head: First-pass encoding notes
div.note: Independent inspection confirms an unfilled initial position before tat and the large interior space before silua. The right-margin incipit is retained separately with schematic abbreviation marks. No missing S or decoration is invented.
Independent source inspection confirms: The line has uultus amantis, with a suspension sign in uultus; e caudata and long-s allographs are treated according to the header policy.
Independent source inspection confirms: The visible opening is In pedibus and the next word is uicii; this witness reading is retained rather than replacing it with a familiar reading.

The opening shows Lidi followed by a raised curled suspension sign, rather than the first-pass full Lidia. It is represented schematically as Lidiꝰ with a qualified Lidius expansion. The final erant remains locally uncertain because of surface disturbance.

The sequence after cantate lacks a secure p descender and does not support the first-pass prius expansion. Enlarged inspection gives a tentative risit; it remains unclear and unexpanded. The small raised stroke is not enough to establish a specific abbreviation.

Independent inspection supports the baseline inuicta and the separate marginal innixa. Both are retained. No deletion stroke establishes a replacement action, so the margin is not silently substituted into the verse.

The group after non has a visible bar and a compact terminal form; the first-pass full potes obscured that abbreviation evidence. The display pot̄u is schematic, with the final character uncertain. No expansion is imposed from another witness.

Enlarged independent reading resolves the opening as Multa, with the same rounded capital-M form seen in Munus60 and Mota69. The following l and t support Multa rather than the first-pass Omnia; the uncertainty is removed.
Independent source inspection confirms: Visible Vel quotiens and illusa pependit are retained as witness wording, without normalization.

The group after Munus consists of h and a c-like form with two small marks above; ḧc is a schematic display. The first-pass contextual hoc expansion is unsupported and has been removed. The final meū suspension supports meum and does not require a user decision.
Independent source inspection confirms: The source has tacto without an encoded con- abbreviation, so no prefix is silently supplied.

The opening is written Qd, not full Quid. The source form is now encoded as an abbreviation; Quod is a qualified contextual expansion. The same Qd form at35 and57 is represented explicitly, with question-context Quid expansions.
The visible Inplebū contraction is retained. Its Inplebunt expansion is now qualified because the written group does not independently establish a final t; no alteration of the source form is made.
The bar in the contracted opening Alt̄a is now explicitly encoded, with expansion Altera. The same visible contraction at65 is represented consistently.
The source writes an abbreviated G with a small o above. It is now represented as an abbreviation with superscript o and expansion Ergo, not as a separately added word or as full written Ergo.
